purpose: select one log-domain Gamma primitive before any later phase is inspected

candidates.name: LOG-ID
candidates.description: shape-boosting identity evaluated on the log scale: log X = log Y + log(U)/a, Y ~ Gamma(a+1,1), U ~ U(0,1)
candidates.attribution: Ahrens & Dieter (1974) for the identity; log-scale use established by Xi, Tan & Liu (2013, doi:10.18637/jss.v055.i04) and Liu, Martin & Syring (2017, doi:10.1007/s00180-016-0692-0)

candidates.name: LOG-PUB
candidates.description: published small-shape acceptance-rejection generator returning log Y, transcribed from Liu, Martin & Syring (2017), Sect. 3, p. 1770
candidates.domain: 0 < a < 1 strictly; outside it the draw falls back to std::gamma_distribution and is flagged out_of_domain

considered_and_not_implemented.name: Xi, Tan & Liu (2013) Algorithm 1
considered_and_not_implemented.reason: ratio-of-uniforms generator valid for all a > 0 whose log-scale delivery is selected by a hard-coded a < 0.01 switch and whose bounding rectangle comes from piecewise-linear tables fitted at efficiency R = 0.9; LOG-PUB is specific to the small-shape regime and has a closed-form acceptance rate that gives an exact check on the transcription

log_w_switch_note: for log W > -30 the regularized incomplete beta is evaluated directly; below it the small-W log form log q = a log W - log a - log B(a,3/2) is used. Both are validated against an mpmath oracle over at least 10 natural-log units on each side of the switch before any sampling result is inspected.
selection_rule: zero avoidable log-domain failures in the pilot
simultaneous distributional tests pass under the frozen familywise rule
every predeclared log-quantile lies inside its acceptance interval
no unbounded retry path or undocumented fallback
exact primary-source attribution and stated parameter domain
tie-break on lower median time per accepted log-Gamma variate unless the faster method has materially greater complexity or weaker documented bounds
